newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss suspected of abusing 1,500 Sri Lanka kids.
newsitem.headline: Swiss suspected of abusing 1,500 Sri Lanka kids.

text.p: A Swiss businessman under investigation on suspicion of sexually abusing around 1,500 children in Sri Lanka was ordered kept in jail by a Swiss judge on Friday.
Zurich district attorney Peter Pellegrini said the judge placed the suspect, 54-year-old Viktor Baumann, under formal arrest.
A native of Zurich resident Sri Lanka for the past eight years, Baumann was taken into custody on Tuesday when he was flew into Zurich after being deported from Colombo.
The order means he can be kept in jail for up to three months while the investigation continues.

"The authorities in Sri Lanka accuse him of having abused around 1,500 children there," Pellegrini said, adding the Swiss probe, based on a complaint from a child welfare group, was running in conjunction with Sri Lankan investigations.
Pellegrini said he had asked Sri Lankan authorities for their records and planned to travel there in March.
Sexual abuse carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison in Switzerland. Baumann could face 10 years in jail if charged and convicted of sexual coercion, Pellegrini said.
Baumann was charged in Sri Lanka with gross indecency and grave sexual abuse of children, police there said.
He was arrested last October in the company of several local children at his house near the coastal resort of Negombo, 24 miles (38 km) north of Colombo.
